receipts.evidence: The only HTML sink is v-html at line 35. userManual is a build-time constant, and every markdown title, paragraph, list, quote, table cell, and inline value reaches renderInline, which calls escapeHtml at lines 50-62 before adding fixed code/strong markup. The section id inserted at line 152 is likewise developer-controlled from userManual.sections; no imported, stored, API, or workspace value reaches the renderer.
The title prop is rendered by Vue interpolation; the panel has no HTML, URL, network, credential, state-mutation, or privileged sink.
Only reads local rotation-group count and navigates to fixed /editor before opening the fixed zoneRotation dialog at lines 76-77; no external input or privileged rotation execution occurs here.

Numeric inputs are normalized with explicit min/max/precision at lines 185-209. Applying a draft requires confirmation at lines 222-236 and mutates only the current workspace through updateConfig; no cross-account, file, network, HTML, or credential boundary is crossed.

Desktop users can replace retieheApiBase at line 15. handleSave persists it at line 219 and immediately calls authenticated updateSyncSettings at line 238; the supporting request layer forwards an origin-agnostic in-memory Cookie jar to that new base.

supporting_files.evidence: cookieJar is global at line 6; setRetieheApiBase at lines 14-16 stores any trimmed string without URL/origin validation or clearing cookies; resolveApiUrl at lines 22-30 concatenates the new base; buildCookieHeader at lines 76-94 serializes all stored session cookies plus the CSRF cookie; apiFetch sets Cookie at line 107 and sends it to the resolved URL at line 122.

Successful SCE authentication leaves token as cookie-session and the desktop cookie jar populated. updateSyncSettings at lines 517-535 requires that existing login, then calls apiFetch with an X-CSRF-Token. clearRetieheSessionCookies is called on logout, not when the API base changes.

WebDAV Basic credentials are sent to the user-selected WebDAV destination as the feature requires. Browser proxy requests use the authenticated dav-proxy; desktop direct requests are an explicitly operator-configured boundary. No separate reportable source-to-unintended-host path was established from this panel.
Lines 30-40 allow plugin-http to all HTTPS destinations and localhost HTTP, so an attacker-controlled HTTPS SCE base is reachable from the desktop runtime.

candidates.title: Changing the desktop SCE API base forwards the previous server's session cookies to the new origin
candidates.attacker_controlled_source: A desktop user can be induced to enter an attacker-controlled HTTPS SCE cloud-service base in SyncPanel. The value is accepted verbatim apart from whitespace and trailing-slash removal.
candidates.broken_control: The desktop cookieJar is global rather than keyed by scheme/host/port. setRetieheApiBase neither validates the destination against the authenticated origin nor clears/rebinds the jar. Consequently an existing session remains active after the authority changes.
candidates.sink: handleSave changes the base and then updateSyncSettings calls apiFetch. apiFetch builds a Cookie header containing the old sce_session and sce_csrf values and sends it via Tauri plugin-http to the newly configured origin.
candidates.impact: The new-origin operator can capture the victim's SCE session and matching CSRF token and replay them against the original SCE service, taking over the victim's authenticated account and accessing or modifying cloud workspaces until the session expires or is revoked.
candidates.why_plausible: The UI performs the base switch before its authenticated save request. The jar deliberately strips Set-Cookie attributes into one process-global map, buildCookieHeader sends every entry, and resolveApiUrl uses the current base. There is no origin comparison or intervening logout. The Tauri capability permits arbitrary HTTPS requests.
candidates.closest_apparent_control: The field is desktop-only and the user explicitly configures a server, but that consent covers data intentionally sent to the configured server, not credentials issued by a different origin. HTTPS protects transport to the attacker-controlled server and does not prevent disclosure. Cookie clearing exists only in logout, so it is mis-scoped for base changes.

validation.method: Full-file source-to-sink review of SyncPanel, apiClient, and useAuth plus Tauri capability reachability.
validation.evidence: SyncPanel lines 219 then 238 establish ordering; apiClient lines 6, 14, 76, 107, and 122 establish origin-agnostic credential forwarding; useAuth line 523 supplies an authenticated request and CSRF header.
validation.recommended_check: With a disposable account, log in to origin A, change the desktop base to a controlled HTTPS origin B, save settings, and confirm B receives A's sce_session and sce_csrf Cookie values. Do not use production credentials.

preconditions: Victim is logged into SCE in the desktop application
Attacker convinces the victim to configure an attacker-controlled HTTPS API base
The existing session has not been logged out or expired
steps: Origin A sets the SCE session cookie, which apiClient stores in the global cookieJar
Victim enters origin B in SyncPanel and clicks save
setRetieheApiBase changes the destination without clearing or partitioning cookieJar
updateSyncSettings immediately invokes apiFetch with a CSRF token
apiFetch attaches the old session and CSRF values to a request sent to origin B
Attacker replays the captured values against origin A
constraints: Desktop/Tauri runtime only; the browser path relies on browser-managed same-origin cookies
Requires user interaction to change the endpoint, but the cross-origin credential forwarding is silent and not necessary for configuring a new server

candidates.severity_context: High account impact with a meaningful user-interaction precondition; likely medium severity after calibration.
